rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the full elution window and identify the limiting pairs while keeping the run close to the 10-minute scoring threshold. Subsequent injections can trim the solvent window and tune slope and temperature.

Lengthen only the gradient to test whether the two limiting pairs respond to a shallower slope. The current last-peak time suggests useful room to improve separation while remaining near or below 10 minutes.

The limiting pair improved strongly with a shallower gradient; narrowing the solvent window should bring its resolution toward 1.5. Raising the starting organic fraction should offset the slower slope enough to keep the last peak below 10 minutes.

Narrow the gradient window further to raise the remaining limiting pair above R = 1.5. The higher starting organic fraction should keep the last peak below 10 minutes, while the first peak should remain sufficiently retained.

Shorten the programmed gradient while preserving the successful starting composition and slope of 0.05 organic fraction per minute. Since all peaks previously eluted before this gradient ends at the outlet, this method should retain CRF 1.000 without the unnecessary high-organic tail.

With the maximum CRF already achieved, test whether a modest temperature increase shortens elution while preserving full resolution. Changing only temperature will reveal its effect on the limiting pair's selectivity.

Test a higher temperature to see whether the limiting pair separates again after an elution-order crossover, potentially giving a shorter fully resolved run. Keep the gradient fixed to isolate temperature-driven selectivity changes; injection 5 remains the maximum-score fallback.

Make the gradient 10% shallower to improve the newly limiting middle pair at 55 C, using the available time margin below 10 minutes. This also tests whether the reordered neighboring pair retains its full-resolution margin.

Use a slope of 0.046875 per minute, between injections 7 and 8, to shorten elution while targeting full resolution. Interpolation suggests the limiting pair should remain above R = 1.5 and the last peak should elute near 9 minutes.

Shift injection 8's solvent window upward while preserving its slope to test whether elution can be shortened without losing full resolution. The early pair has some resolution margin, but the middle pairs will determine whether the higher starting organic fraction is beneficial.

Test a hotter, steeper gradient for a substantially shorter fully resolved run, potentially separating the troublesome middle pair on the other side of an elution-order crossover. The maximum CRF is already secured, so this injection explores a faster alternative rather than refining the established method.

Increase gradient steepness at fixed temperature and starting composition to test whether the reordered limiting pair separates further beyond its crossover. This explores a faster maximum-score method, while checking that compression does not create another unresolved pair.

Test an intermediate temperature and slope to balance the two temperature-sensitive middle separations. This targets a faster fully resolved method without the severe compression seen in injection 12.

Explore cooler-temperature selectivity with a moderately steep gradient, since the warmer fast methods retain a limiting middle pair. This tests a distinct route to a shorter fully resolved separation while preserving the established CRF 1.000 methods as fallbacks.

Combine the favorable 55 C selectivity with a lower starting organic fraction to improve the middle-pair separation that deteriorated when phi0 increased. The steeper gradient targets a shorter run than injection 9 while testing whether stronger initial retention preserves full resolution.

Slightly reduce the slope from injection 15 to test whether its narrow resolution margins can be improved while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes. This targets a more robust maximum-score method rather than additional speed.

Test an intermediate starting composition and slope to balance the two limiting middle pairs. This should offer better resolution margins than injection 15 while retaining a shorter separation than injection 9.

Increase the slope slightly from injection 17, from 0.0625 to 0.065 per minute, to shorten elution while retaining full resolution. The observed margins suggest this is a useful test near the fastest fully resolved boundary for this starting composition.

Return to the successful 40 C selectivity and shift the solvent window upward while preserving injection 5's slope. This tests whether the cooler method can elute faster without sacrificing its limiting middle pair or compressing the early pair below R = 1.5.

Test 35 C with a steeper gradient to explore whether cooler-temperature selectivity can resolve the middle cluster in a shorter run. This samples the gap between the unfavorable 30 C result and the successful 40 C region, with maximum-score methods already secured.

Use a slightly shallower gradient than injection 17 to improve the weaker middle separation while retaining the favorable 55 C selectivity. This targets a balanced resolution margin at CRF 1.000, with the last peak expected comfortably below 10 minutes.

Slightly flatten injection 8's gradient to test whether both limiting pairs can retain stronger resolution margins while the last peak remains below 10 minutes. The theoretical maximum score is already secured; this targets a less marginal maximum-score alternative.

Increase the slope slightly from the fastest fully resolved method, injection 15, to test its speed limit. This should shorten the last-peak time, although the middle pair at R = 1.59 may fall below full resolution; injection 15 remains the faster maximum-score fallback.

Test a 5 C temperature increase from the fastest fully resolved method, injection 15, while keeping its gradient fixed. This checks whether the lower starting organic fraction supports a faster maximum-score separation at 60 C, despite the selectivity limitations seen with higher starting organic.

Use a slope of 0.04444 per minute, between injections 8 and 22, to balance the two limiting pairs near R = 1.7 while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. This final injection targets a stronger resolution margin at the already-achieved maximum CRF of 1.000.
